function: Receiver MIMO detection by deep-unfolded OAMP-CDT for a SIM-enabled transmitter; the SIM layers (diffractional channel coding) are fixed from prior work, not learned (p. 4, 8, 10).
system: Point-to-point MIMO: transmissive stacked SIM transmitter (3 layers, 49 meta-atoms per layer, G=4 RF chains) at 28 GHz; receiver M=7 antennas, also 32x32 (p. 3, 11).
method: Deep-unfolded OAMP with trainable scaling parameters plus causal dilated convolution and multi-head attention modules (OAMP-CDT); supervised, cross-entropy loss per iteration, Adam, 10 unfolding iterations (p. 8, 9, 11).
data_channel: Simulated: i.i.d. and exponential-correlation Rayleigh channels; 3GPP 3D MIMO channels from QuaDRiGa v2.2.1 for Fig. 8; 80k training, 20k test realizations; no measured data (p. 11, 12, 14).
test_conditions: Rayleigh training at random SNR 5-15 dB, QPSK/16-QAM, tested on same channel type; correlation and DCC cases trained separately; 3GPP dataset (Fig. 8); SNR 0-20 dB model also tested (p. 12, 14, 15).
baselines: Non-learned: OAMP, MMSE, ML detectors; learned: OAMP-Net2 (deep-unfolded OAMP [23]) (p. 11, 12).
metrics: Symbol error rate (SER), analytic versus simulated SINR PDF and CDF, convergence versus iterations, complexity order, average latency (p. 11, 12, 13).
complexity: Table II: complexity orders, OAMP-CDT O(T(MG^2+G^3+G ch)+HG^2); Table III: latency 304 us for OAMP-CDT versus 268 us OAMP-Net2 at 7x7 (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 14: "a dataset comprising authentic channel samples acquired from the 3GPP 3D MIMO channel [46]", generated with the QuaDRiGa simulator [47] (p. 15; Table I, p. 11); p. 11: "we also employ a more realistic MIMO scenario using 3GPP channel matrices [46]". The main results use Rayleigh channels (p. 12).
q2_support: p. 14: "Following training, the network is evaluated using the corresponding channel correlation coefficients" (same distribution); p. 15: "Both models were tested within 0 - 20 dB under QAM-16 modulation" is an SNR sweep. No train-test mismatch in scenario, antennas or channel type is stated.
q3_support: p. 11: "comparing it with OAMP [41], OAMP-Net2 [23], ML, and MMSE detectors"; p. 12: "OAMP-CDT exhibits advantages of 2.00 dB, 0.28 dB, and 2.84 dB compared to the OAMP, OAMP-Net2, and MMSE, respectively" in SER.
q4_support: p. 11: "Table II summarizes the computational complexities of the three baseline methods in comparison with the proposed OAMP-CDT algorithm" and "Table III presents the average latency of different detectors under a 7 × 7 MIMO configuration".
q5_support: p. 12: "We establish a dataset comprising training and validation sets with 80k channels": the data are self-generated; p. 11 names only Python 3.9 and TensorFlow 2.10; no code or data link, public dataset or measurement is mentioned.
notes: The PDF is the paper of the DOI (p. 1: Digital Object Identifier 10.1109/TWC.2026.3679383). ris is 1 because the transmitter is a stacked intelligent metasurface (p. 3, 11); its layers are not optimized (p. 4, footnote 2), so the learned function is receiver detection, area 1. q1 uses the 3GPP 3D MIMO channel (reference [46] is TR 36.873) generated with QuaDRiGa v2.2.1, not TR 38.901 itself, and the paper does not say whether the detectors in Fig. 8 were trained on it or on Rayleigh channels (p. 14, 15); if trained on Rayleigh, q2 would be 1. Reviewer to confirm. Tables I to III read from the page image (p. 11).
